'openClaw does so muhc more then Claude code tbh, running 9 agents from the one machine, schedual some tasks, add some personal personas for each agent, claudeCode... is on rails, openClaw is full openworld.'
1Password blog flagged that the top skill available for OpenClaw was recently a malware installer, per 'From Magic to Malware: How OpenClaw's Agent Skills Become an Attack Surface'.
'I spent the weekend comparing nanoclaw to openclaw - nanoclaw is a slightly more secure version - containerized filesystem basically... has almost exactly the same security risk surface.'
'The openclaw security model is the equivalent of running as root - i.e. full access.' Commenter calls this standard security 101 but notes it's inherently risky.
'For me, personal home IT chores that I've put off for years... Got it done in a couple hours with openclaw.' User praised OpenClaw for automating home infrastructure setup.
'I haven't found ANY uses for it where it actually did what it was supposed to do.'
Users reported Claude Code would refuse requests or trigger extra usage billing simply from commit messages mentioning 'OpenClaw', reproducible via a simple git commit test.
Anthropic emailed Claude Code subscribers saying third-party tools like OpenClaw 'put an outsized strain on our systems' and would no longer be usable with Claude Code subscriptions, only via API.

'OpenClaw was still using Claude Code as the harness (via claude -p)... Anthropic is doing this... building products around claude -p is disallowed' per docs.openclaw.ai on the Anthropic provider option.
Google restricted Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers from using OpenClaw with their subscriptions, compared by a commenter to 'ISPs banning customers in the 90s for using Napster'.
